name: [WEEKLY] AI/LLM Agent Framework Runtime Spawning Shell, Recon, or Egress Child Process
description: Detects a public-facing AI/LLM agent-framework runtime (Langflow/uvicorn, PraisonAI AgentOS, LobeHub, Crawl4AI, Rclone rcd, or the npm/Node MCPServer) spawning an OS shell, reconnaissance utility, or network-egress tool — the post-exploitation behaviour that turns an unauthenticated RCE primitive into hands-on-keyboard execution. It matters this fortnight because a cluster of CRITICAL GHSAs landed against these frameworks (CVE-2026-48519 'Langflow Shareable Playground RCE', CVE-2026-55450 'Langflow unauthenticated upload', CVE-2026-49980 'Rclone rcd inline-remote command exec', CVE-2026-54157 'LobeHub /webapi/proxy SSRF', the PraisonAI Jobs-API/AgentOS/MCPServer/AgentTeam.launch unauthenticated-invocation set, and 'Crawl4AI Chromium launch-argument injection') — all exploit T1190 then pivot to T1059, and the IOCs (endpoints, ports) differ per product so only the parent→child execution chain generalises. It spans the exploit and install kill-chain stages: the framework process is the initiating parent, the shell/LOLBin is the child. It fires when one of these runtimes (or a Chromium child launched with --no-zygote plus a subprocess-launcher switch) directly spawns sh/bash/cmd/powershell/curl/wget/nc/whoami and similar; it does NOT fire on normal agent inference, model downloads via the framework's own HTTP client, or interactive developer shells whose parent is a terminal rather than the server runtime. Because these frameworks have no legitimate reason to fork a system shell in production, the parent-child pair is alert-grade.
